title: Mariner Bay Medical Center: Hurricane Vertical Evacuation of NICU and ICU
summary: A 310-bed hospital in Corpus Christi, Texas, and its hurricane and critical care evacuation plans, with an exercise generated from them: a Category 3 hurricane forecast to bring 34-knot winds at 18:00 Wednesday, a 12-hour clearance time, a late horizontal evacuation decision and the vertical movement of the NICU and ICU with short staffing.
notice: EXERCISE MATERIAL — for training use. Mariner Bay Medical Center, its people, units, vendors and sites are simulated; the storm is fictional; the public sources consulted for realism are listed in reference/gulf-coast-nursing/SOURCES.md.

scenarios.title: Clearance Time
scenarios.summary: A Category 3 hurricane is forecast to bring tropical-storm-force winds to Corpus Christi at 18:00 the next day; the horizontal evacuation deadline is 12 hours before that, the hospital's elevators and staffing are marginal, and the nurses must move 12 NICU infants and 19 ICU patients upward in priority order while keeping handoffs, ratios and family communication intact.
